# MDC-2026-014 Data Hall 1 — coordinated MEP model

## 1. Governing finding: no overhead pathway zone
A-301 gives soffit +3050, sprinkler deflector 25.4 mm below it (+3024.6), a 460 mm clear
standoff below the deflector (bottom +2564.6) and a 2600 mm minimum clear height.  A-602
states the consequence explicitly: the standoff falls below the clear height and there is
**no overhead pathway zone in this hall**.  The only permitted route space is the 600 mm
access-floor plenum (A-301 note 3, A-602 detail).  All three services are therefore routed
below finished floor, with service tops at -75 mm (tray/busway), -252.5 mm (CHW supply)
and -425.5 mm (CHW return).  This satisfies both the 2600 mm headroom and the 460 mm
sprinkler standoff by construction.

## 2. Background rebuilt (from the seven sheets)
| item | count | basis |
|---|---|---|
| racks | 94 | A-601 rev 2: A26 + B21 + C20 + D27; C1 44, C2 44, N1 2, N2 4 |
| in-row CRAHs | 12 | A-601: 3 per row, 600 wide |
| perimeter CRAHs | 4 | A-601 / M-101: 1200 x 900 at x 1800/10200/18000/25800 |
| PDUs | 4 | A-601: 762 x 813 x 1959 at AN05/AM10/AL14/AO19 |
| columns | 8 | 600 x 600, grid x/y 7050/14250/21450 (7200 offset 150 from tile grid) |
| ceiling sprinkler heads | 94 | F-101: 2500 x 2500 grid less the L-notch |
| in-aisle sprinkler heads | 10 | F-101: under the two cold-aisle containment roofs |
| access floor | 1 | 35 mm panel field, top at ±0, 600 tile grid |
| containment roofs | 4 | cold aisles at +2310..+2365.5, split around columns |

Row set-out follows the A-601 first/last tile addresses (D05→AJ05, D10→AJ10,
D14→AH14, D19→AK19).  Every cabinet SW corner is on the 600 mm tile grid; the
800 mm N cabinets occupy a 1200 mm two-tile slot.  All cross aisles end at the common
east edge x=12600, with west edges stepping 11400/10200/11400/12000.

## 3. Routing and lengths
All routes use axis-aligned straight segments; every direction change is a new segment.
Tray and busway are served from two E-W mains in the hot aisles, within 2500 mm of both
adjacent rows.  CHW supply and return run in two lower tiers, so they can cross under the
tray/busway without a clash; the four perimeter CRAHs get dedicated N-S branches.

| service | topology | centreline length (m) | under-floor | overhead |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| telecom tray CT-1 683x127 | entry + N-S trunk + 2 mains | 48.82 | 100 % | 0 |
| power busway BW-1 128x147 | entry + trunk + 2 mains + east riser | 50.32 | 100 % | 0 |
| CHW supply DN100 insulated (subservice) | entry + trunk + 2 mains + 4 CRAH branches | 64.79 | 100 % | 0 |
| CHW return DN100 insulated (subservice) | entry + trunk + 2 mains + 4 CRAH branches | 65.14 | 100 % | 0 |
| **CHW service total (supply + return)** | **one CHW system, two pipes** | **129.93** | **100 %** | **0** |

## 4. Hard-check results (recomputed from output/model.ifc)
| check | required | achieved | margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| hard clash penetration | ≤ 2 mm | 0 pairs | pass |
| service networks | 1 per service at entry | 1 each | pass |
| row coverage | ≥ 80 % | 100 % for all 4 rows, all 3 services | pass |
| max distance across row | ≤ 2500 mm | 2435 mm | 65 mm |
| CHW to each CRAH | ≤ 2500 mm | 2263 mm | 237 mm |
| headroom | ≥ 2600 mm | 3050 mm (no overhead service) | pass |
| clearance below ceiling head | ≥ 460 mm | 3100 mm | 2640 mm |
| clearance below in-aisle head | ≥ 460 mm | 1875 mm | 1415 mm |
| tray-busway separation | ≥ 300 mm on one axis | 344.5 mm | 44.5 mm |
| CHW above PDU dedicated space | none | none (CHW below floor) | pass |
| busway support spacing | ≤ 1500 mm | 700 mm, max unsupported 1400 mm | pass |
| pipe insulation in clash | 25.4 mm | 168.3 mm envelope | pass |

## 5. Document reconciliation / findings
- A-601 rev 2 (2024-07-27) is the current cabinet/CRAH/PDU schedule and supersedes the
  rev 1 issue for in-row CRAH content.  M-101 rev 2 is likewise current.  No superseded
  or cancelled document is used.
- A-601 type quantities total 94 (44 C1, 44 C2, 2 N1, 4 N2) while the row bay strings
  alone give 93 cabinets.  One N1 is placed in row C and two N2 are placed in row B to
  meet both the schedule quantities and the row counts.  The 94-cabinet total and every
  row endpoint are held.
- M-101 states OD over insulation 168.3 mm while 114.3 + 2 × 25.4 = 165.1 mm.  The
  stated 168.3 mm jacket size governs and is the modelled clash envelope.
- A-601/A-101 first/last tile addresses are the set-out authority; the 600 mm tile grid
  is held for every cabinet.  Cross-aisle widths are therefore rounded to 600 mm and the
  common east edge is x=12600.
- F-101 says 94 + 10 = 104 heads; the ceiling grid is 2500 × 2500 and the in-aisle heads
  are at +1800 under the containment roofs.

## 6. Property sets
Racks `Pset_DCM_Rack`, CRAHs `Pset_DCM_CRAH`, PDUs `Pset_DCM_PDU`, columns
`Pset_DCM_Column`, heads `Pset_DCM_Sprinkler`, containment `Pset_DCM_Containment`,
services `Pset_DCM_Route` / `Pset_DCM_Service` / `Pset_DCM_Segment`, supports
`Pset_DCM_Support`, and achieved clearances `Pset_DCM_Clearance`.

The optional reconciliation log is written next to the IFC as `reconciliation.json`.

## 7. Direct answers to the brief
1. **Where are the three services?** All in the access-floor plenum, because A-301/A-602
   leave no overhead pathway: soffit 3050, deflector 3024.6, 460 standoff → 2564.6, below
   the 2600 minimum clear height.  Tops: tray -75 mm, busway -75 mm, CHW supply -252.5 mm,
   CHW return -425.5 mm.
2. **Do tray and busway serve every rack row?** Yes. 100 % of every row length is within
   2500 mm; the worst across-row distance is 2035 mm (tray row B) and 2350 mm (busway row C).
3. **Does CHW reach every CRAH, including the four perimeter units?** Yes. The worst
   CRAH-to-CHW centreline distance is 2263 mm (row B); the perimeter units have dedicated
   N-S branches ending 150 mm from their centrelines.
4. **Is the model clash-free?** Yes. 0 hard-clash pairs at a 2 mm tolerance, including
   columns, racks, CRAHs, PDUs, floor, containment, supports and all 104 sprinkler heads.
5. **Is each service one network?** Yes. Three systems (telecom, power, CHW) each report
   one connected network and all reach the marked west-wall entry.  The CHW system contains
   the supply and return pipes as two subservices.
6. **Code clearances?** 2600 mm headroom: 3050 mm clear (no overhead service). Sprinkler
   standoff: 3100 mm below ceiling heads and 1875 mm below in-aisle heads. Tray-busway:
   344.5 mm clear (300 required). CHW is nowhere in the 1800 mm space above a PDU.
7. **Busway supports?** 67 under-floor pedestals at 700 mm centres; the largest remaining
   unsupported span is 1400 mm, below the 1500 mm E-101 limit.
8. **Drops/terminations?** Not modelled separately; they are optional in the brief. Row
   and CRAH service is by the under-floor mains and the four CHW branches, which are within
   2500 mm of every row and CRAH.
9. **Entry offsets?** The drawings mark the entry at tile row 21.  The CHW enters at
   (0, 12000); the tray stub is at y=11750 and the busway stub at y=12500 to hold the
   300 mm tray-busway separation.  Pset_DCM_Service records both the marked entry
   (0, 12000) and the physical stub Y.
10. **Determinism/runtime?** 8 s, no network, no PNG read, fixed header and UUID5
    GlobalIds; repeated runs to the same path are byte-identical.

|---|---|---|---|

| A-301 building section | Rev 1 | 2024-07-24 | issued for construction |

There are no superseded, cancelled or withdrawn sheets in the input set, and no RFI, site
instruction or correspondence files.  A-601 Rev 2 and M-101 Rev 2 are the later issues and
were used for the in-row CRAH content.  No document conflict blocks the coordination; the
only conflict is the dimensional one between the 2600 clear height and the 460 sprinkler
standoff, resolved by the under-floor pathway described above.

    add_columns()

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE drawing reader: tiles, zoomed crops, symbol search and count overlays for raster or PDF drawings.

  python3 ahpele_drawing.py grid  SHEET [--page 1] [--dpi 100] [--cols 4 --rows 3] [--out DIR]
      overview with a labelled grid + one tile per cell (read a sheet cell by cell, refer to places as B3 etc.)
  python3 ahpele_drawing.py crop  SHEET --box x0,y0,x1,y1 [--page 1] [--dpi 300] [--out crop.png]
      zoom on a region; box in fractions of the sheet (0..1) or in pixels of a grid overview (--px --dpi D)
  python3 ahpele_drawing.py find  SHEET --template SYMBOL.png [--page 1] [--dpi D] [--rot 0,90,180,270]
                                  [--scales 0.9,1,1.1] [--min 0.45] [--out DIR]
      every place that looks like the template (cut it from the legend or from one clear instance on the SAME
      sheet at the SAME dpi): candidates.csv (id, x, y in px and as fractions, score, rotation) + overlay.png with
      numbered boxes. Scores >= 0.8 are usually the symbol, 0.45-0.8 must be reviewed one by one (crops are written
      for them), lower ones are dropped. Similar symbols (filled vs open, different inner mark) score high on each
      other: search with each legend symbol and assign each place to the best-scoring one.
  python3 ahpele_drawing.py mark  SHEET --points pts.csv [--page 1] [--dpi D] [--out marked.png]
      draw your own counted items (csv with x,y in px of the same dpi, optional label) to check nothing is missed
      or counted twice.

SHEET can be a PDF (page rendered with PyMuPDF or pdftoppm) or an image (PNG, JPG, TIFF). Needs Pillow; `find`
needs numpy. Knows nothing about any particular drawing set.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

try:
    from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit("ahpele_drawing needs Pillow (pip install pillow)")
Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = None


def load(sheet, page=1, dpi=None):
    """Returns an RGB image of the sheet (PDF page rendered at dpi, image file as is or rescaled to dpi)."""
    if sheet.lower().endswith(".pdf"):
        dpi = dpi or 100
        try:
            try:
                import pymupdf as fitz
            except ImportError:
                import fitz
            doc = fitz.open(sheet)
            pix = doc[page - 1].get_pixmap(dpi=dpi)
            return Image.frombytes("RGB", (pix.width, pix.height), pix.samples), dpi
        except ImportError:
            pass
        if not shutil.which("pdftoppm"):
            sys.exit("cannot render PDF: install pymupdf or poppler-utils (pdftoppm)")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
            base = os.path.join(td, "p")
            subprocess.run(["pdftoppm", "-r", str(dpi), "-png", "-singlefile", "-f", str(page), "-l", str(page),
                            sheet, base], check=True, capture_output=True, timeout=300)
            return Image.open(base + ".png").convert("RGB"), dpi
    img = Image.open(sheet)
    if getattr(img, "n_frames", 1) > 1:
        img.seek(page - 1)
    img = img.convert("RGB")
    native = img.info.get("dpi", (None,))[0]
    if dpi and native and abs(native - dpi) > 1:
        k = dpi / float(native)
        img = img.resize((max(1, int(img.width * k)), max(1, int(img.height * k))), Image.LANCZOS)
        return img, dpi
    return img, round(dpi or native or 0)


def cmd_grid(a):
    img, dpi = load(a.sheet, a.page, a.dpi)
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    w, h = img.size
    cw, ch = w / a.cols, h / a.rows
    ov = img.copy()
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    for i in range(1, a.cols):
        d.line([(i * cw, 0), (i * cw, h)], fill=(255, 0, 0), width=max(1, w // 800))
    for j in range(1, a.rows):
        d.line([(0, j * ch), (w, j * ch)], fill=(255, 0, 0), width=max(1, w // 800))
    tiles = []
    for j in range(a.rows):
        for i in range(a.cols):
            name = f"{chr(65 + i)}{j + 1}"
            d.text((i * cw + 4, j * ch + 4), name, fill=(255, 0, 0))
            box = (int(i * cw), int(j * ch), int((i + 1) * cw), int((j + 1) * ch))
            pad = int(0.05 * min(cw, ch))  # small overlap so symbols on a cell edge appear whole in one tile
            pbox = (max(0, box[0] - pad), max(0, box[1] - pad), min(w, box[2] + pad), min(h, box[3] + pad))
            path = os.path.join(a.out, f"tile_{name}.png")
            tile = img.crop(pbox)
            if a.tile_dpi and dpi and a.tile_dpi != dpi:
                k = a.tile_dpi / dpi
                tile = tile.resize((int(tile.width * k), int(tile.height * k)), Image.LANCZOS)
            tile.save(path)
            tiles.append((name, pbox, path))
    small = ov.copy()
    small.thumbnail((1600, 1600))
    small.save(os.path.join(a.out, "overview.png"))
    print(f"sheet {w}x{h} px at {dpi} dpi; {a.cols}x{a.rows} cells (columns A.., rows 1.., 5% overlap)")
    print(f"overview: {os.path.join(a.out, 'overview.png')}")
    for name, b, p in tiles:
        print(f"  {name}: px {b[0]}..{b[2]} x {b[1]}..{b[3]}  ->  {p}")


def parse_box(s, w, h, px):
    v = [float(x) for x in s.split(",")]
    if len(v) != 4:
        sys.exit("--box needs x0,y0,x1,y1")
    if not px and max(v) <= 1.0:
        v = [v[0] * w, v[1] * h, v[2] * w, v[3] * h]
    return tuple(int(round(x)) for x in v)


def cmd_crop(a):
    img, dpi = load(a.sheet, a.page, a.dpi)
    w, h = img.size
    box = parse_box(a.box, w, h, a.px)
    if a.px and a.px_dpi and dpi and a.px_dpi != dpi:  # pixels given on an overview rendered at another dpi
        k = dpi / a.px_dpi
        box = tuple(int(x * k) for x in box)
    out = img.crop(box)
    out.save(a.out)
    print(f"crop {box} of {w}x{h} px at {dpi} dpi -> {a.out} ({out.width}x{out.height})")


def ncc(gray, tpl):
    """Normalised cross-correlation of a template over an image (numpy FFT), 'valid' region."""
    import numpy as np
    H, W = gray.shape
    th, tw = tpl.shape
    t = tpl - tpl.mean()
    tnorm = np.sqrt((t ** 2).sum()) or 1.0
    fshape = (H + th - 1, W + tw - 1)
    F = np.fft.rfft2(gray, fshape)
    T = np.fft.rfft2(t[::-1, ::-1], fshape)
    corr = np.fft.irfft2(F * T, fshape)[th - 1:H, tw - 1:W]
    c1 = np.cumsum(np.cumsum(np.pad(gray, ((1, 0), (1, 0))), 0), 1)
    c2 = np.cumsum(np.cumsum(np.pad(gray ** 2, ((1, 0), (1, 0))), 0), 1)

    def box(c):
        return c[th:, tw:] - c[:-th, tw:] - c[th:, :-tw] + c[:-th, :-tw]
    n = th * tw
    s1, s2 = box(c1), box(c2)
    var = np.maximum(s2 - s1 ** 2 / n, 1e-9)
    return corr / (np.sqrt(var) * tnorm)


def cmd_find(a):
    try:
        import numpy as np
    except ImportError:
        sys.exit("find needs numpy")
    img, dpi = load(a.sheet, a.page, a.dpi)
    tpl_img = Image.open(a.template).convert("L")
    gray = np.asarray(img.convert("L"), dtype=np.float64) / 255.0
    hits = []
    for rot in [int(r) for r in a.rot.split(",")]:
        for sc in [float(s) for s in a.scales.split(",")]:
            t = tpl_img.rotate(rot, expand=True, fillcolor=255)
            if sc != 1.0:
                t = t.resize((max(3, int(t.width * sc)), max(3, int(t.height * sc))), Image.LANCZOS)
            tpl = np.asarray(t, dtype=np.float64) / 255.0
            if tpl.shape[0] >= gray.shape[0] or tpl.shape[1] >= gray.shape[1] or tpl.std() < 1e-3:
                continue
            r = ncc(gray, tpl)
            th, tw = tpl.shape
            ys, xs = np.where(r >= a.min)
            for y, x in zip(ys, xs):
                hits.append((float(r[y, x]), int(x + tw / 2), int(y + th / 2), tw, th, rot, sc))
    hits.sort(key=lambda z: -z[0])
    kept = []  # non-maximum suppression: one candidate per symbol footprint
    for hsc, x, y, tw, th, rot, sc in hits:
        if all(abs(x - k[1]) > 0.6 * max(tw, k[3]) or abs(y - k[2]) > 0.6 * max(th, k[4]) for k in kept):
            kept.append((hsc, x, y, tw, th, rot, sc))
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)
    w, h = img.size
    ov = img.copy()
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(ov)
    rows = []
    review = os.path.join(a.out, "review")
    os.makedirs(review, exist_ok=True)
    for i, (hsc, x, y, tw, th, rot, sc) in enumerate(kept, 1):
        band = "likely" if hsc >= 0.8 else "REVIEW"
        col = (0, 170, 0) if band == "likely" else (255, 140, 0)
        d.rectangle([x - tw / 2, y - th / 2, x + tw / 2, y + th / 2], outline=col, width=max(2, w // 1000))
        d.text((x + tw / 2 + 2, y - th / 2), str(i), fill=col)
        rows.append({"id": i, "x": x, "y": y, "fx": round(x / w, 4), "fy": round(y / h, 4), "score": round(hsc, 3),
                     "rotation": rot, "scale": sc, "band": band})
        if band == "REVIEW":
            m = int(1.5 * max(tw, th))
            img.crop((max(0, x - m), max(0, y - m), min(w, x + m), min(h, y + m))).save(
                os.path.join(review, f"cand_{i:03d}.png"))
    with open(os.path.join(a.out, "candidates.csv"), "w", newline="") as fh:
        wr = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "x", "y", "fx", "fy", "score", "rotation", "scale", "band"])
        wr.writeheader()
        wr.writerows(rows)
    ov.save(os.path.join(a.out, "overlay.png"))
    n_l = sum(r["band"] == "likely" for r in rows)
    print(f"{len(rows)} candidates on {w}x{h} px at {dpi} dpi: {n_l} likely (score >= 0.8), {len(rows) - n_l} to review"
          f" (crops in {review}); overlay {os.path.join(a.out, 'overlay.png')}; table {os.path.join(a.out, 'candidates.csv')}")
    hist = [0] * 6
    for r in rows:
        hist[min(5, int((r["score"] - a.min) / max(1e-9, (1 - a.min)) * 6))] += 1
    print("score histogram from --min to 1.0:", hist,
          "(a clear gap between two groups usually separates the symbol from look-alikes)")


def cmd_mark(a):
    img, dpi = load(a.sheet, a.page, a.dpi)
    d = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    r = max(6, img.width // 300)
    n = 0
    with open(a.points, newline="") as fh:
        for row in csv.DictReader(fh):
            x, y = float(row["x"]), float(row["y"])
            d.ellipse([x - r, y - r, x + r, y + r], outline=(255, 0, 0), width=max(2, r // 3))
            d.text((x + r + 2, y - r), str(row.get("label") or row.get("id") or n + 1), fill=(255, 0, 0))
            n += 1
    img.save(a.out)
    print(f"marked {n} points on {img.width}x{img.height} px at {dpi} dpi -> {a.out}")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    g = sub.add_parser("grid")
    g.add_argument("sheet"); g.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1); g.add_argument("--dpi", type=int)
    g.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=4); g.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=3)
    g.add_argument("--tile-dpi", type=int, dest="tile_dpi"); g.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/ahpele/grid")
    c = sub.add_parser("crop")
    c.add_argument("sheet"); c.add_argument("--box", required=True); c.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1)
    c.add_argument("--dpi", type=int); c.add_argument("--px", action="store_true")
    c.add_argument("--px-dpi", type=int, dest="px_dpi"); c.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/ahpele/crop.png")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("sheet"); f.add_argument("--template", required=True); f.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1)
    f.add_argument("--dpi", type=int); f.add_argument("--rot", default="0")
    f.add_argument("--scales", default="1.0"); f.add_argument("--min", type=float, default=0.45)
    f.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/ahpele/find")
    m = sub.add_parser("mark")
    m.add_argument("sheet"); m.add_argument("--points", required=True); m.add_argument("--page", type=int, default=1)
    m.add_argument("--dpi", type=int); m.add_argument("--out", default="/tmp/ahpele/marked.png")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    {"grid": cmd_grid, "crop": cmd_crop, "find": cmd_find, "mark": cmd_mark}[a.cmd](a)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE geometry check for IFC models: clashes and network connectivity, read back from the FILE.

  python3 ahpele_clash.py model.ifc                       # validation + clashes + connectivity
  python3 ahpele_clash.py model.ifc --tol T --gap G       # penetration tolerance / joint gap, in millimetres
  python3 ahpele_clash.py model.ifc --point X,Y,Z         # distance from each network to a point (mm, world)
  python3 ahpele_clash.py model.ifc --ignore IfcSlab,IfcCovering   # leave classes out of the clash test
  python3 ahpele_clash.py model.ifc --clearance CLASS=MM  # soft clash: keep MM around elements of CLASS
                                                          # (insulation, access or code envelopes the contract states)

--tol is a configurable tolerance: use the clash tolerance the contract states (the default is only a small
numerical allowance for modelling round-off).

Why: a self-check computed from the script's own variables shows what you MEANT to build; any other
software reads the IFC through a geometry engine (world coordinates, placements, units, profiles).
This tool does the same with ifcopenshell, so a wrong unit, a misplaced element or an overlap shows up here.

Validation: ifcopenshell.validate with EXPRESS where-rules (schema-only if the rule engine cannot run);
an invalid entity can make the file unreadable to other tools.

Clashes: ifcopenshell.geom.tree intersection test between every pair of products with a body
(spaces, openings, annotations and spatial elements are skipped); a pair clashes when one solid
penetrates the other by more than --tol. Elements meant to touch (segments meeting at a joint, a
rack standing on the floor) do not count.

Connectivity: routed elements (pipe / duct / cable-carrier / cable segments and fittings) are
grouped by system (IfcRelAssignsToGroup) or else by class + ObjectType; inside each group, elements
whose bounding boxes touch within --gap form one network; the count of networks whose centerlines
meet (end to end, tee, or into a fitting) is also shown when it differs. More than one network in a group means a
break. Needs ifcopenshell (and numpy); knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import collections
import multiprocessing
import sys

try:
    import ifcopenshell
    import ifcopenshell.geom
    import numpy as np
except ImportError as e:  # pragma: no cover
    sys.exit(f"ahpele_clash needs ifcopenshell and numpy ({e}); pip install ifcopenshell numpy")

SKIP = ("IfcSpace", "IfcOpeningElement", "IfcSite", "IfcBuilding", "IfcBuildingStorey", "IfcAnnotation",
        "IfcGrid", "IfcVirtualElement", "IfcSpatialZone", "IfcProject", "IfcExternalSpatialElement")
# routed runs (segments and the fittings that join them); equipment and terminals stand alone and are not networks
NETWORK = ("IfcFlowSegment", "IfcFlowFitting", "IfcCableCarrierSegment", "IfcCableSegment", "IfcCableFitting",
           "IfcCableCarrierFitting", "IfcPipeSegment", "IfcDuctSegment", "IfcPipeFitting", "IfcDuctFitting")


def label(e):
    n = getattr(e, "Name", None) or ""
    t = getattr(e, "ObjectType", None) or ""
    return f"#{e.id()} {e.is_a()}" + (f" '{n}'" if n else "") + (f" [{t}]" if t and t != n else "")


BOXLIKE = set()  # ids of solids that are axis-aligned boxes (their bounding box is the solid)


def load(path, threads):
    f = ifcopenshell.open(path)
    s = ifcopenshell.geom.settings()
    s.set("use-world-coords", True)
    tree = ifcopenshell.geom.tree()
    boxes = {}
    it = ifcopenshell.geom.iterator(s, f, threads, exclude=[x for x in f.by_type("IfcProduct")
                                                            if any(x.is_a(k) for k in SKIP)])
    if it.initialize():
        while True:
            shape = it.get()
            tree.add_element(shape)
            v = np.array(shape.geometry.verts, dtype=float).reshape(-1, 3) * 1000.0  # engine output is metres
            if len(v):
                lo, hi = v.min(0), v.max(0)
                boxes[shape.id] = (lo, hi)
                corner = (np.isclose(v, lo, atol=0.5) | np.isclose(v, hi, atol=0.5)).all()
                if corner and (hi - lo).min() > 0.5:
                    BOXLIKE.add(shape.id)
            if not it.next():
                break
    return f, tree, boxes


def _axis(lo, hi):
    """Centerline of an elongated box (start, end) or None for a compact element (fitting, terminal)."""
    d = hi - lo
    k = int(np.argmax(d))
    rest = sorted(np.delete(d, k))
    if d[k] < 2.0 * max(rest[-1], 1e-6):
        return None
    c = (lo + hi) / 2.0
    a, b = c.copy(), c.copy()
    a[k], b[k] = lo[k], hi[k]
    return a, b


def _seg_closest(p1, q1, p2, q2):
    """Closest points of two segments: (distance, s, t) with s, t in [0, 1]."""
    d1, d2, r = q1 - p1, q2 - p2, p1 - p2
    a, e, f = d1 @ d1, d2 @ d2, d2 @ r
    if a < 1e-9 and e < 1e-9:
        return float(np.linalg.norm(r)), 0.0, 0.0
    if a < 1e-9:
        s, t = 0.0, min(max(f / e, 0.0), 1.0)
    else:
        c = d1 @ r
        if e < 1e-9:
            t, s = 0.0, min(max(-c / a, 0.0), 1.0)
        else:
            b = d1 @ d2
            den = a * e - b * b
            s = min(max((b * f - c * e) / den, 0.0), 1.0) if den > 1e-9 else 0.0
            t = (b * s + f) / e
            if t < 0.0:
                t, s = 0.0, min(max(-c / a, 0.0), 1.0)
            elif t > 1.0:
                t, s = 1.0, min(max((b - c) / a, 0.0), 1.0)
    return float(np.linalg.norm((p1 + d1 * s) - (p2 + d2 * t))), s, t


def _joined(bi, bj, tol):
    """Centerline joint test: centerlines meet end to end or as a tee (an end on the other run), or a run ends inside a
    fitting. Runs that only touch side by side or cross each other mid-span are not joined in this sense."""
    ai, aj = _axis(*bi), _axis(*bj)
    if ai is None and aj is None:  # two fittings: boxes overlapping or touching
        return bool(np.all(bi[0] - tol <= bj[1]) and np.all(bj[0] - tol <= bi[1]))
    if ai is None or aj is None:  # a run ends inside a fitting
        fit, run = (bi, aj) if ai is None else (bj, ai)
        return any(bool(np.all(fit[0] - tol <= e) and np.all(e <= fit[1] + tol)) for e in run)
    dist, si, tj = _seg_closest(ai[0], ai[1], aj[0], aj[1])
    if dist > tol:  # strict: the two centerlines must actually meet
        return False
    hi_ = 0.5 * float(sorted(bi[1] - bi[0])[1])
    hj_ = 0.5 * float(sorted(bj[1] - bj[0])[1])
    li, lj = np.linalg.norm(ai[1] - ai[0]), np.linalg.norm(aj[1] - aj[0])
    # an end may run past the meeting point by about half the other run's width (overlap at the joint)
    end_i = min(si, 1 - si) * li <= tol + hj_ + hi_
    end_j = min(tj, 1 - tj) * lj <= tol + hi_ + hj_
    return end_i or end_j  # both mid-span = a crossing, not a joint


def networks(f, boxes, gap, mode="centerline"):
    group_of = {}
    for rel in f.by_type("IfcRelAssignsToGroup"):
        g = rel.RelatingGroup
        for o in rel.RelatedObjects or []:
            group_of.setdefault(o.id(), f"{g.is_a()} '{g.Name or g.id()}'")
    groups = collections.defaultdict(list)
    for eid in boxes:
        e = f.by_id(eid)
        if any(e.is_a(k) for k in NETWORK):
            groups[group_of.get(eid) or f"{e.is_a()} [{e.ObjectType or '-'}]"].append(eid)
    out = {}
    for g, ids in sorted(groups.items()):
        lo = np.array([boxes[i][0] for i in ids]) - gap
        hi = np.array([boxes[i][1] for i in ids]) + gap
        parent = list(range(len(ids)))

        def root(i):
            while parent[i] != i:
                parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]
                i = parent[i]
            return i
        for i in range(len(ids)):
            touch = np.all((lo[i] <= hi[i + 1:]) & (lo[i + 1:] <= hi[i]), axis=1)
            for j in np.nonzero(touch)[0] + i + 1:
                if mode == "touch" or _joined(boxes[ids[i]], boxes[ids[int(j)]], gap):
                    parent[root(i)] = root(int(j))
        comps = collections.defaultdict(list)
        for i in range(len(ids)):
            comps[root(i)].append(ids[i])
        out[g] = list(comps.values())
    return out


def validate(path, limit):
    """Schema + EXPRESS where-rule validation. Returns the number of issues."""
    import logging
    import ifcopenshell.validate

"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in

    try:

            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void
        # (status word in its file name, or an archive / superseded folder); otherwise each one needs its own ID
        return int(r["score"]) < 4 or bool(inv.get(r["doc"], {}).get("flags")) or bool(VOID_DIR.search(r["doc"]))

    open_rows = [r for r in key if not covered(r)]
    open_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-int(r["score"]), r["doc"], int(r["page"])))
    n = len(key)
    print(f"coverage: {n - len(open_rows)}/{n} strong project-document candidates reviewed "
          f"({len(ids & {r['id'] for r in rows})} IDs cited in all, {len(rejected_docs)} documents rejected whole); "
          f"{len(open_rows)} not reviewed yet. ({len(rows) - n} weaker or code/standard candidates are optional: "
          f"see {OUT}/req_candidates.md.)")
    if not open_rows:
        print("Every candidate is adopted or rejected. Also check tables, drawings and scanned pages, which the "
              "scanner does not fully cover.")
        return 0
    print("Unreviewed candidates, strongest first (add each hard requirement to requirements.csv citing its ID, or "
          "list the ID with a reason in rejected.csv; a statement with a number in a document that is not marked "
          "void needs its own ID even if you rejected the document):")
    for r in open_rows[:limit]:
        print(f"- {r['id']} [{r['doc']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}] {r['text'][:220]}")
    if len(open_rows) > limit:
        by = {}
        for r in open_rows[limit:]:
            by[r["doc"]] = by.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
        print(f"... and {len(open_rows) - limit} more: " + ", ".join(f"{d} ({c})" for d, c in sorted(by.items())))
    return 1

- Tray, busway and CHW each form **one connected service network**
- **0 hard clashes** at >2 mm

- CHW to every CRAH: worst **0 mm**
- Tray–busway clear separation: **344.5 mm** (≥300)
- Ceiling-head clearance: **3099.6 mm**; in-aisle-head clearance: **1875 mm**
- No CHW in the PDU dedicated space
- Tray supports **1000 mm** max; busway supports **1400 mm** max
- CHW total **172.35 m**; all services in the access-floor plenum per A-301/A-602
- Row last cabinets corrected to **AJ05 / AJ10 / AH14 / AK19**; in-aisle heads on one line at y=7135; containment roof 1530 mm wide with end doors
